author_stated_preferences.comment_verbatim: One thing I don't like with either is the long lists. Lists of more than three things are offensive to me, and multiple lists in a paragraph are also offensive and appear as word filler. Example: "how information is represented, where a boundary belongs, how to check a result, and what happens when separately sensible components meet. "
author_stated_preferences.scope: Strong objection to long prose enumerations and multiple enumerations in a paragraph; the supplied example is an inline enumeration.

implementation_hypotheses_not_yet_genera: Select the examples needed for the point or express their supported relationship; splitting a long list into several lists would not address the stated objection.
A three-item limit alone does not ensure good prose: R03 criticizes a three-item setup too. Judge what the enumeration contributes.
Preserve useful explanations while reconsidering irrelevant caveats with the author; a source-preserved caveat may itself need factual correction.
Check whole-piece narrative continuity separately from word-level correction; local fixes do not by themselves establish a better story.
